title: Decompose packed-support canonicalization and remove redundant Boolean-value assembly
hypothesis: GPU-09 showed that final canonical TypedRelationBlock materialization dominates the packed Boolean one-shot path. Split that boundary into packed-support decoding and canonical block construction before adding another backend or cache, and remove the redundant per-entry Boolean values list because packed support already implies True.

finding.classification: materialization remains dominant; constructor validation is material
finding.summary: The existing baseline now measures packed-support decode separately from canonical TypedRelationBlock construction while preserving total canonicalize_ms. Across all six frozen cases, canonicalization consumed about 56-93 percent of the packed one-shot path. At 256 nodes / requested density 0.05, support decode took 9.355059 ms and block construction 11.224812 ms, for 20.579871 ms canonicalization inside a 22.189957 ms one-shot path. Therefore the boundary cost is not only bit scanning; canonical block validation/construction is itself material.
finding.next_architectural_implication: Do not add a cache, alternate relation object, trusted constructor, or another arithmetic backend yet. First measure which existing TypedRelationBlock validation/canonicalization checks account for construction cost and determine whether safe reuse can avoid duplicate work without weakening the canonical oracle.

gardener.reason: measurement wire semantics gained an explicit canonicalization phase split
gardener.redundancy_removed: packed-support decoding no longer accumulates a values list with one True per output edge; the canonical Boolean values tuple is constructed once from the decoded entry count

interpretation: All six baseline cases retained exact Boolean support and canonical digest equality against the stdlib CSR oracle.
Canonicalization remains the dominant one-shot cost in the larger/dense cases even after removing redundant Boolean-value list assembly.
TypedRelationBlock construction is a material part of canonicalization, so optimizing only packed-bit scanning cannot remove the boundary cost.
Cross-run timing differences versus older artifacts are not treated as a speedup because hosted-run noise was not controlled as a paired experiment.
